_about: Marcus Aurelius in English, translator per title: George Long (1862), George W. Chrystal (1902), clean Gutenberg. The Adler shelf's marcus-meditations (PG 2680) is labelled 'tr. George Long' there, but PG 2680 names no translator and its text opens 'His First Book concerning Himself', Meric Casaubon's 1634 wording, in an Everyman-style edition whose introduction lists Long as a different translator; so it is cross-referenced as Casaubon (inferred, not stated by the file). Older translations from the wishlist added 2026-10-02 as raw IA OCR (translator per row).

marcus-aurelius-chrystal: The Meditations of the Emperor Marcus Aurelius Antoninus: a new rendering

marcus-aurelius-collier: The Emperor Marcus Antoninus, his Conversation with Himself (1702)
marcus-aurelius-jackson-1906: The Meditations of Marcus Aurelius Antoninus (Oxford, Frowde, 1906; introduction by Charles Bigg)
tr. John Jackson (from the catalogue; the scan's title page names no translator)
marcus-aurelius-casaubon-everyman: The Meditations of Marcus Aurelius (Everyman's Library no. 9, intro. W. H. D. Rouse; first issue of this edition 1906, this scan the 1948 reprint)
marcus-aurelius-collier-1701: The Emperor Marcus Antoninus his Conversation with Himself, with Gataker's preliminary discourse and Dacier's Life (London: Richard Sare, 1701)
marcus-aurelius-collier-zimmern-1887: The Meditations of Marcus Aurelius (Camelot Series; London: Walter Scott, 1887)
tr. Jeremy Collier, revised by Alice Zimmern

marcus-aurelius-casaubon-everyman.rights_override: Imprint read: 'First issue of this edition 1906, Last reprinted 1948' (Dent/Dutton). Casaubon's translation is of 1634 and Rouse's introduction of 1906; a reprint adds nothing new. Taken as the 1906 edition, US public domain. Rouse died in 1950, so the introduction is not public domain everywhere under life+70.
